correctness.rationale: The exact weighted-normal coordinate norm follows from the grounded Laplacian orthogonal projector; by acyclic path decomposition each unit flow is a convex mixture of routes. Each edge antichain yields an upper bound for a feasible inball radius. A proof of weighted Dilworth by integer replication, rational scaling, and compactness constructs a matching path mixture and shows equality, the full optimal-center inequalities, and sharp antichain tangencies. Exact rational computations of 678 coordinate norms in 96 graph/metric profiles and independent route LPs corroborate the proof.

A complete-DAG radius theorem restricts graph and netflow and so does not dominate arbitrary acyclic DAGs and positive metrics.

originality.rationale: Same-object literature (arXiv:2101.10425, arXiv:2203.01896, arXiv:2205.09168) treats routes, triangulations, Ehrhart structure, and volume, not the stated effective-resistance/weighted-antichain intrinsic inradius for all DAG unit flows and the full incenter locus. A restricted previously inspected complete-DAG inball is a special case rather than a theorem over all DAGs and metrics. The known network projector and Dilworth principle do not independently assert the resulting metric theorem. Priority provisional because a generic poset-packing LP result might imply the formula.
residual_risks: An earlier published Chebyshev-center theorem for chain-mixture polytopes, weighted antichain covering, or arbitrary network flows may imply an equivalent statement without referring to resistance or flow-polytopes by name.
Review of literature was targeted, not a complete historical census; independent expert validation is not represented.

value.rationale: The result gives a natural exact geometric invariant for every acyclic source–sink network, converts a continuous inball optimization problem into an electrical-network calculation and a weighted poset antichain computation, classifies all incenter locations, and identifies compulsory tangent coordinate hyperplanes. The arbitrary-network and all-center components are structural, not an isolated family’s arithmetic.
